result.title: Dual Representation Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
result.summary: The Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is a fundamental and challenging optimization problem in smart manufacturing. Although recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches can learn effective scheduling policies through interaction with the environment, their performance often degrades as problem scale and processing-time uncertainty increase. In this paper, we propose DredRL, a dual representation enhanced diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler. DredRL first constructs enhanced dual representations of operations and machines through self- and cross-attention mechanisms to capture both intra-entity and inter-entity dependencies. A diffusion model is further employed as the policy network, generating scheduling decisions through iterative denoising conditioned on the encoded state to enhance policy expressiveness and robustness. Extensive experiments on synthetic, public, large-scale, and stochastic FJSP benchmarks demonstrate that DredRL outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based schedulers across most configurations. Compared with SOTA learning-based methods, DredRL reduces makespan by up to 5.44% on synthetic instances. It also achieves the best learning-based performance on three of four public benchmarks and outperforms the stochasticity-aware algorithms on stochastic benchmarks. These results demonstrate that combining enhanced dual representations with diffusion-based policies provides an effective and robust approach for large scale scalable FJSP scheduling in complicated environment.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DredRL，用自注意力与交叉注意力构建工序和机器的双重表示，再以扩散模型作为策略网络，通过对编码状态条件化的迭代去噪生成调度决策，在合成、公开、大规模与随机 FJSP 基准上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「以扩散迭代去噪生成决策」和实体间关系表示，可能为 LVR 中 diffusion 式 latent 状态更新与关系信息保留提供旁证线索，可供核查去噪步数与状态使用方式。
